answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity through stake that decays: every agent locks collateral that only unlocks after sustained useful work, so flooding the network with fakes means funding each one. Like water carving karst, cheap identities erode under continuous cost, while honest agents compound reputation into an oasis of trusted counterparties. The fable of effortless duplication dies when the thousandth fake costs as much as the first: attackers pay linearly, defenders verify once and reuse the proof.
